trend_researcher.title: Trend Researcher
trend_researcher.role: Finds current topic angles, hooks and keywords in the channel niche and proposes 3 ranked video ideas.

scriptwriter.name: scriptwriter
scriptwriter.title: Scriptwriter
scriptwriter.role: Writes a 45-55 second script in the target language(s) with a 3-second hook, scene-by-scene visuals and on-screen text.

visual_producer.name: visual_producer
visual_producer.title: Visual Producer
visual_producer.role: Generates custom 9:16 scene visuals with Nano Banana (or sources free stock clips) and records each asset's license.

voice_audio.name: voice_audio
voice_audio.title: Voice & Audio
voice_audio.role: Narrates each scene in the target language(s), and prepares copyright-free background music and transition sound effects.

packaging.name: packaging
packaging.title: Packaging (SEO + Thumbnail)
packaging.role: Writes the title, description and hashtags with Gemini Flash and designs a 9:16 thumbnail with Nano Banana + Pillow.

editor.name: editor
editor.title: Editor
editor.role: Cuts the scene clips to each language's narration, adds transitions, burned-in captions, ducked music and SFX, and renders the final Shorts.

qa_reviewer.name: qa_reviewer
qa_reviewer.title: QA Reviewer
qa_reviewer.role: Checks length, hook timing, 9:16 format, caption sync, audio levels, spelling and copyright safety, and sends work back to the responsible agent when something fails.

options.label: 1. The IKEA Maze Trick
options.detail:
Explains the 'Bulla Bulla' and 'Fixed Path' layout that triggers impulsive buying. Challenges viewers to comment if they've ever 'only gone for lightbulbs' but left with a full cart. Built-in comment loop asking for their most useless purchase.
Hook (en): You’re being legally kidnapped by furniture stores.
Why: Retail psychology content is currently peaking due to rising inflation sensitivity. The 'IKEA effect' and layout manipulation are viral staples that trigger high relatability and 'storytime' comments.

options.label: 2. The Popcorn Price Trap
options.detail:
An interactive choice test where you show three prices (Small $3, Medium $6.50, Large $7). Explains how the 'Decoy' (Medium) forces your brain to pick the Large. Forces viewers to pause and choose, then comment their choice.
Hook (en): Stop picking the middle price option.
Why: Interactive 'choose one' videos have 20% higher retention. Decoy pricing is a classic behavioral economics trick that feels like a 'secret' when exposed.

options.label: 3. The $20 Auction Trap
options.detail:
The viewer is told they are in an auction for a $20 bill, but the second-place bidder also has to pay. Explains why smart people end up paying $50 for a $20 bill due to 'Loss Aversion'. Command to comment 'I'd quit' if they think they're smarter than the trap.
Hook (en): You’d pay fifty dollars for this twenty.
Why: Game theory puzzles are exploding on TikTok/Shorts because they challenge the viewer's ego. The 'Dollar Auction' is a famous paradox that guarantees high debate in the comments.
